correctness.rationale: The derived ideal is precisely V, so any automorphism is (e ↦ ce+w, v ↦ Tv) with TA=cAT; conversely this sole bracket constraint and invertibility suffice. Determinant forces c²=1, trace forces c=1 except in the trace-zero case, and finite-field perfection excludes irreducible trace-zero quadratics in characteristic two. Identify V with E=F_(q²), A with multiplication by λ. The c=1 centralizer consists of multipliers u∈E×; T−I is invertible for u≠1 and otherwise the translation column has rank zero or one. Thus the bins in order 0,1,2,3 are (0,q²(q²−2),q²−1,1). For odd trace zero, λ^q=−λ and the c=−1 solutions are exactly u times Frobenius. Fixed vectors then lie in V. In the basis 1,λ, writing λ²=d and u=x+yλ, the semilinear map has matrix [[x,−dy],[y,−x]] and det(T−I)=1−N(u). The norm-one fiber has q+1 elements, and T−I cannot be zero since tr(T)=0≠2. Each T has q² independent translations. This adds (q²(q+1)(q−2),q²(q+1),0,0), exactly giving the second column and fixed-point-free fraction after dividing by 2q²(q²−1). This also handles q=2 and q=3 without exceptions. The submitted checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed; their ten finite configurations are corroborative, not the all-field argument.

value.rationale: The fixed-space census is a natural refinement of the automorphism group order and of fixed-point-free existence for a standard nonsplit family. It exhibits exactly how the quotient scalar and the norm-one condition change the distribution in the trace-zero case, and quantifies the characteristic-two obstruction. It supplies the multiplicities needed for fixed-vector and derangement questions, not merely a classification label or a few small-field values.
